citeAs: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan (2022). Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. NeurIPS 2022.
creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan (University of California Los Angeles, Arizona State University, Allen Institute for AI)
description: ScienceQA is a large-scale multimodal multiple-choice science question answering dataset containing 21,208 examples collected from elementary and high school science curricula. It covers diverse topics across three subjects (natural science, social science, and language science) spanning 26 topics, 127 categories, and 379 skills. Most questions are annotated with grounded lectures and detailed explanations that serve as chain-of-thought reasoning annotations.
name: ScienceQA
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Lectures and explanations were sourced directly from IXL Learning's existing annotations. For human performance evaluation, Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with high school or higher degrees answered test questions; workers had to correctly answer 4 out of 5 qualification examples to qualify. Each batch of 10 test questions was answered by 3 different workers. For human evaluation of generated explanations, AMT workers rated explanations on relevance, correctness, and completeness; human scores were determined by majority vote.
rai:dataCollection: Questions in the ScienceQA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards. Individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted from downloaded science problems using heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed, answer options were shuffled, and semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science problems from IXL Learning, an online K-12 education platform. The raw data includes questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions aligned with California Common Core Content Standards.
rai:dataLimitations: Current multimodal models fail to understand fine-grained visual information in images (especially diagrams), and image captions used as visual input lack fine-grained semantics. Models also struggle with complex domain-specific knowledge. There is a 20.07% gap between human performance and the best model for image-context questions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Invalid questions were manually removed (questions with only one choice, questions with faulty data, and duplicate questions). If there were multiple correct answers, only one was kept. Answer options were shuffled to ensure choices do not follow any specific pattern. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions so that special structures (tables, lists) are distinguishable from simple text. Incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts using a data exploration tool.
rai:dataSocialImpact: ScienceQA is proposed to diagnose multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems. It does not contain user usage data or personally sensitive information. The dataset will contribute to K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. Any antisocial data points will be removed based on feedback.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmark for multimodal learning, multi-hop reasoning, and general artificial intelligence research. Development of K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. Studying chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 (available at https://huggingface.co/nlpconnect/vit-gpt2-image-captioning) was used to generate captions for images in the dataset as visual context for language models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. The dataset does not contain personally identifiable information or offensive content.

evidence.rai:dataUseCases: SCIENCE QA provides a useful benchmark for multi-modal learning, multi-hop reasoning, and general artificial intelligence. Besides, SCIENCE QA will contribute to the development of K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. Furthermore, the designed methods with the chain of thought investigate the ability of large language models to mimic the human mind process when reasoning about a challenging task.
evidence.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The collected data does not contain personally identifiable information or offensive content.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: We extract the image captions and feed them to the large language model as the visual content input. However, these captions lack fine-grained semantics and usually do not work well for diagrams, which results in two failure cases shown in Figure 17a and 17b. Moreover, there exist challenges for large language models to reason about the questions that require them to understand complex and uncommon domain knowledge.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: We extract the caption from the captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 for the image as the visual context. The maximum length of generated captions is 16, the number of beams is 4, and the maximum number of output tokens is 512.
